mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate higher short-term interest rates and adjust discount rates downward on future earnings.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the preceding month's returns (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS increases are not persistent across 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in UNRATE for three consecutive months indicate labor market softening, which reduces the real wage growth expected by firms and dampens equity discounting, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 70% of UNRATE decline episodes, or the average 60-day return during UNRATE declines exceeds the average during expansions (paired t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (home sales index) above its 12-month moving average coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as rising housing demand signals economic recovery and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 5-day average prior to the HOUST spike (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below its 12-month average, followed by a rebound above that level within the next 20 days, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates improving supply-side conditions.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in > 40% of INDPRO bottoming episodes (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in PAYEMS (employment months) above the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in UNRATE, suggests a transition to a more labor-market-healthy environment and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > prev_month Payne and UNRATE < prev_month UNRATE
failure_condition: The joint signal is present but 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in > 50% of such episodes (bootstrap CI does not include zero).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for two consecutive months during a recessionary regime (as defined by GDP < potential GDP), the S&P 500 tends to exhibit positive 60-day forward returns as expectations of prolonged easing persist.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.0 and GDP < GDP_potential and FEDFUNDS < prev_month_FEDFUNDS
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not consistently positive across 5 such regimes (pooled t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 7% for three consecutive months is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as higher wage growth erodes real earnings and reduces equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in > 80% of such episodes (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in INDPRO—first a sharp decline below its 12-month average, then a rapid recovery above it within 5 trading days—predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates supply-chain normalization.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in > 70% of such double-dip episodes (rolling window).
